task.description: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (WF-02 Step 1b) hard gate on REQ-183's design artefact at lib/letflow/design/req183-webhook-delivery-dispatch.md (webhook delivery dispatch core: deliver/3, webhook_delivery_attempts schema/migration, HMAC signing, retry/backoff, auto-pause, DLQ landing). Verify every acceptance criterion below maps to a concrete design element, no fenced code block reproduces real .ex implementation (signatures/type-shapes only are acceptable), and the plaintext-secret-for-HMAC architectural question is resolved explicitly (SS0) rather than silently assumed -- including that the design correctly states REQ-190/Letflow.Secrets does not exist yet in this tree and names the build-sequencing precondition.
acceptance_criteria: deliver/3 against a target_url returning 200 persists one webhook_delivery_attempts row with status "SUCCESS", http_status_code 200, and does not increment the subscription's consecutive_failures

deliver/3 against a target_url returning 500, and separately against one that refuses the connection outright, both persist a row with status "FAILED" and last_error populated (http_status_code 500 for the first, null for the connection-refused case) -- two explicit tests

deliver/3's signature is independently verifiable: a test computes the expected HMAC-SHA256 signature from the same secret and payload and asserts it equals the value deliver/3 actually sent in the documented header -- and the design states exactly how deliver/3 obtains that secret (Letflow.Secrets.resolve/2, not a plaintext field on Subscription)
a subscription's consecutive_failures reaching the documented threshold flips its status to "PAUSED" and sets paused_at -- driven by repeated failed attempts and read back afterward
a delivery exhausting max_attempts lands exactly one entry in REQ-176's DLQ core with entry_type "webhook" and reference_id equal to the delivery's own delivery_id, read back from the DLQ table

the moduledoc names the HMAC header/format and the PAUSED-threshold number as Letflow's own choices, explicitly not ported from R-Co's src/webhook/ (unreachable from this drafting session), and names automatic post-event triggering as an explicitly deferred follow-up rather than silently implemented or silently omitted
no route or controller file is added or modified, confirmed by git diff --stat scoped to this requirement's commits

the design explicitly resolves the plaintext-secret-availability architectural question (does not silently assume plaintext is available) and states precisely why the resolution does not defeat REQ-181's original security intent

the design states plainly that Letflow.Secrets/REQ-190 does not exist yet in this tree, cites what it is designed against instead (REQ-190's own design artefact, not a guess), and states the build-sequencing precondition for ELIXIR-DEV's Step 2a
no fenced code block in the design artefact reproduces real, executable .ex implementation -- signatures/type-spec-only blocks are acceptable
